body: OK no problem. Just to give more context. I indeed traced back the problem when we trigger the blur to all input. This is triggered because there is a "popstate" and the state is different. This popstate is correctly triggered in modern browsers with the use of history API, and it is triggered when the URL is manipulated directly in the bar or using back or forward history buttons. But it is emulated when we use the hash, using hashchange event. This is event is triggered whatever the way the url is modified. Because of that we make a test, but it is not full proof against fast typers, as the state in the helper keep being modified even though we don't have yet the search results :(
